artboards.title: A — Duration leads, severity as a figure
B — Severity leads, with a scale

annotations.text:
A — Duration leads, severity as a figure

Closest to what ships. Duration stays the headline; severity becomes a real figure with the app's severity ramp carrying magnitude, and the peak sits beside it as the quiet number.

Tradeoff: safest, least distinctive. Colour is the only thing doing visual work.

The severity and peak sliders above the frame change every mockup on it — worth pushing severity to 2 and to 9 to see the ramp switch.

Shipping today, for comparison

All four states as they render on the phone right now. Everything is one of two text sizes, so nothing leads — this is the flatness you spotted.

B — Severity leads, with a scale

Severity is the hero and duration demotes to a corner. The 10-step scale gives magnitude a position, not just a colour, and marks the peak as an outlined tick — readable without reading a number.

Tradeoff: the scale is close to a progress bar, which is a shape that implies a goal. Worth checking it doesn't read as one.

C — Trajectory

Reuses the sparkline already on every Logs row (y pinned 0–10, line coloured by the peak). Shows where the attack has been, not just where it is — the peak becomes a shape rather than a second number.

Tradeoff: needs data the widget payload does not carry yet — the readings, not just now and peak. A real change, not just a redraw. Also the least legible at a glance of the three.

All four are drawn in Lexend. The shipping widget uses the system face (SF) — the app's own type spec never crossed into the extension. Worth deciding either way; it is a small change to bundle the font into the widget target.
